what_its_for: Voxelotor is used to treat sickle cell disease in adults and children who are at least 4 years old. It works by helping your red blood cells hold onto oxygen better and keep their normal round shape, so they are less likely to become stiff and sickle-shaped. This helps reduce the breakdown of red blood cells and improves anemia caused by sickle cell disease.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet or take the dissolved powder by mouth once a day, with or without food. Tablets should be swallowed whole — do not crush, cut, or chew them. If you are taking the powder for oral solution, mix the packet with 60 mL (about 2 ounces) of water or milk and stir well, then drink it right away. Do not save it for later. Take voxelotor at about the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing 40 kg (about 88 pounds) or more is 1,500 mg (three 500 mg tablets) once a day. Children weighing less may take a lower dose as directed by their doctor. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes — do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 8 hours since your usual dose time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 8 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store voxelotor tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store the powder packets at room temperature as well. Keep all medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking voxelotor with certain medicines that can affect how it works in your body. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, including herbal supplements. St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) and certain seizure, antibiotic, or antifungal medicines can interact with voxelotor. Avoid starting any new medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any serious side effects, including: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, rash, hives, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel dizzy, have severe diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach ache, headache, or a rash that does not go away. These could be signs of a serious reaction.
when_it_works: You may not feel different right away, but voxelotor starts working to improve your red blood cells within a few weeks. Your doctor will check your blood (hemoglobin levels) after about 4 weeks and regularly after that to see how well the medicine is working. Some people notice improvements in energy and fewer symptoms of anemia over time. Keep taking it every day even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before taking voxelotor, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Children as young as 4 years old can take voxelotor, but the dose will be adjusted based on their weight. If you have liver problems, your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Always tell your doctor your full medical history before starting this medication.
